description:
Page v3 ruling (user 2026-11-18, verbatim via Optimize): "a, b approved. continue to stack." Page: https://claude.ai/artifact/MmnrdprbWQMF24ejqsUaQL (decision A).

%{^key => value} in a case pattern (and in function heads and receive, wherever a map pattern is allowed) matches on interp, run and build, as in Elixir. Today compiler2 rejects it: 'compiler2 case patterns require literal map keys' (src/dispatch_matrix/pattern.rs map_key). Region::MapKeyPresent carries a GroundValue through the matrix, reachability, canon, the interpreter and receive.

This is an Elixir-parity gap in its own right. It is how Elixir writes Map.get/3, replace/3 and update/4, and the compiled match learns of a miss the way the matcher does (a null word tested inline). It replaces a get-with-default or {:ok, v}-building runtime entry, which would have been a second mechanism.

Design page first, to the user before any build. Builder: Optimize, stacked on #761.

comments.text: AUTHORIZED DEFERRAL (the user's ruling 1: 'whichever gets us there faster'). Step 1 is pushed with the single-clause closure head 'fn %{^key => v} -> v end' still refused. It binds through RequireMapValue, which #753 (fz-sc8.248.1) deletes. Once the stack is rebased over #753, that form is accepted and joins fixture 01767. This ticket stays open until it does.

title: A map pattern's key may be a pinned variable
